answer: Each agent must post a unique bond in a shared vault before it can claim rewards, and the bond is slashed if independent auditors prove that identities coordinate as one operator. A sparrow-sized account gets no special exemption: creating thousands of names means locking thousands of bonds and risking their loss. The ocean of possible identities therefore does not translate into free voting power; the attacker pays real capital up front and faces a measurable penalty when caught.
